# Locked-column grids number ARIA rows and columns per region

## Context

A grid with locked columns renders each record in up to three bodies (start, center, end), and each body has its own `role="row"` per record. I found this while checking a blog claim about the grid's ARIA support (`#20184`). On the [issues showcase](https://neomjs.com/dist/production/examples/grid/issues/index.html), `#` and Title are locked at the start and State at the end. A DOM read on neomjs.com production on 2026-10-31 shows:

- `role="grid"` carries `aria-colcount="8"` and `aria-rowcount="498"`.
- The header is three `role="row"` elements, all `aria-rowindex="1"`. Their buttons carry `aria-colindex` 1, 2 | 1 to 5 | 1.
- Every record is three `role="row"` elements, one per `role="rowgroup"` body, sharing one `aria-rowindex`. Their cells carry `aria-colindex` 1, 2 | 1 to 5 | 1. Three cells per record claim column 1, and columns 6 to 8 never appear.
- `src/grid` and `src/draggable/grid` contain no `aria-owns`.

A single-region grid is correct. The [bigData example](https://neomjs.com/dist/production/examples/grid/bigData/index.html) (20,000 rows, 51 columns) has one rowgroup and global `aria-colindex`. Scrolled to its middle, its 32 DOM rows carry `aria-rowindex` 9,997 to 10,028.

The same showcase shows two structure problems that apply to any grid using these features:
- The 13.3 search toolbar (a textbox and buttons) sits inside the `role="grid"` element.
- The header menu triggers (for example "Filter Type") sit inside the header `role="row"` beside the `role="columnheader"` button, not inside a column header.

Checked and fine: the content-sized-rows measure layer (`div.neo-grid-row-measure`) is `aria-hidden="true"` and `visibility: hidden`.

How it happened: the grid's ARIA indices arrived with the buffered grid in January 2025 (`#6175` `aria-rowindex`, `#6176` `aria-rowcount`, `#6187` `aria-colindex`), when a grid had one body, so counting within the body was counting within the grid. The locked-column regions came later (the Grid Multi-Body epic #9486; `lockedStart` lands in `0401f40ea0`, 2026-03-16, `#9457`) and split the grid into up to three bodies, each still counting from 1. The operator confirmed the order: ARIA support came before locked columns.

## The Problem

WAI-ARIA 1.2 rules these out:
- `aria-colindex` "Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid". Authors MUST set it "greater than the aria-colindex value of any previous elements within the same row, and less than or equal to the number of columns in the full table."
- For `aria-rowindex`, authors MUST set it "greater than the aria-rowindex value of any previous rows".
- A `row` owns `cell`, `columnheader`, `gridcell` and `rowheader`. A `grid` owns `row`, directly or through `rowgroup`.

So a screen reader on a locked-column grid gets the wrong column position for every cell outside the start region. It sees each record as three rows, and it finds toolbar controls and menu buttons inside the grid's rows.

## The Architectural Reality

- Body cells: `src/grid/Row.mjs:293` sets `'aria-colindex': columnIndex + 1`, and `columnIndex` counts within the cell's region body (the class `neo-locked-end-first-column` is set when `columnIndex === 0`).
- Header buttons: `src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs:283` and `src/grid/header/Wrapper.mjs:149-150` number them per toolbar. `Wrapper.mjs:141-142` says why: "Buttons carry a toolbar-local aria-colindex, which the header SortZone resolves column positions through at drag start". `src/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs:178` and `:519` read it back (`me.dragElement['aria-colindex'] - 1`), and `:434` writes it.
- `src/grid/Container.mjs:1717` sets `aria-colcount` to `columns.count`, which counts every region. `role: 'grid'` (`Container.mjs:200`) sits on the container, which also holds `searchToolbar_` (`Container.mjs:164`).
- The region bodies pool rows in the same record order: rows with equal `aria-rowindex` across the three rowgroups show one record.

Design authority: WAI-ARIA 1.2 (quoted above), plus the grid's own global `aria-colcount` (`Container.mjs:1717`). The only record of the per-region index (`Wrapper.mjs:141-142`) names it SortZone's lookup channel, not ARIA intent.

## The Fix

1. **Decouple SortZone from ARIA.** SortZone resolves the dragged column from a non-ARIA source, such as the header item's index within its toolbar or its `dataField`, so the ARIA indices can be global.
2. **Global `aria-colindex`.** Each region offsets its cells and header buttons by the column count of the regions before it: start 0, center the start count, end the start plus center counts.
3. **One ARIA row per record.** Candidate: the first present region's row owns the other regions' cells for that record through `aria-owns`, and the other regions' rows take `role="none"`. Owned elements follow the DOM children, so start → center → end order holds. The header rows get the same treatment. Pooled rows recycle in place, so each pool slot's ID list stays stable. Validate with a real screen reader before choosing. If `aria-owns` proves unreliable, record the result and the chosen alternative in the PR.
4. **Grid-owned structure only: moved to #20188.** The search toolbar and the header menu triggers apply to every grid, not only locked ones, and the fix restructures the header element, so it has its own ticket.

Row ownership needs one more step. The start body renders before the other regions build their row pools, and a lead row whose record did not change skips its next render. So each sibling region re-syncs the lead rows' `aria-owns` after its own pass (`Body#syncAriaRowOwns`). `Body#getRecordByRowId` reads the row's own `rowIndex`, because rows outside the lead region carry no `aria-rowindex`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a grid with start and end locked columns, every cell's and header's `aria-colindex` equals its visual column position across regions (1 to N, with N = `aria-colcount`), unique within a row.
- [ ] Column drag and drop, including across regions, works unchanged, and SortZone reads no ARIA attribute.
- [ ] In the browser's accessibility tree, each record exposes one row with all its cells in visual order, and the header exposes one row. A spec covers it: Chromium's tree through CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` on the issues showcase.
- [ ] Single-region grids are unchanged: in bigData, `aria-colindex` stays global and `aria-rowindex` stays one per record.
- [ ] Post-merge: a screen-reader read (VoiceOver with Safari, or NVDA with Firefox or Chrome) on the deployed issues showcase announces the right column header and position for a locked-start, a center and a locked-end cell.

## Out of Scope

- Keyboard navigation across split bodies (#9496).
- Cross-window region detachment (#9493). When a region lives in another window, each window has its own ARIA tree; this ticket does not address it.
- The Table (`src/table`), which uses one `<table>` with sticky locked cells.
- The search toolbar and the header menu triggers inside the grid's rows (#20188).

## Avoided Traps

- **One `role="grid"` per region.** Each region's indices become valid, but a screen-reader user meets three grids for one table.
- **Keeping per-region numbering with a column count per rowgroup.** `aria-colcount` belongs to the grid, not to rowgroups.
- **Reading layout back from ARIA.** The SortZone coupling is how the per-region numbering became load-bearing. ARIA stays write-only for the engine.

* fix(grid): one ARIA grid across locked regions (#20187)

A grid with locked columns renders each record in up to three bodies.
Each body numbered its columns from 1 and gave every record its own
role="row", so a screen reader heard the wrong column outside the start
region and three rows per record.

Columns now count grid-wide: Container#getAriaColumnOffset gives each
region the count of the regions before it, for cells and header

the dragged column by dataField, and Body#getRecordByRowId reads the
row's own rowIndex.
